landing.faq.a1: Pingory is an uptime monitoring service that continuously checks your websites, APIs, servers, and domains. It alerts you the moment something goes down, so you can respond before your users notice.
landing.faq.a2: Sign up for free → click Add monitor → choose the type (HTTP, SSL, Ping, etc.) → enter your URL or hostname → set the check interval → add alert channels (email, Slack, etc.) → save. Takes about 30 seconds.

landing.faq.a4: Yes! The Free plan gives you 50 monitors with 5-minute checks forever—no credit card required. You can upgrade to Starter ($4/month) or Pro ($6/month) anytime for faster checks and more features.
landing.faq.a5: Email alerts are included on all plans. Starter adds Slack, Telegram, and Webhook. Pro adds Discord, Microsoft Teams, and PagerDuty. You can configure multiple channels per monitor.
landing.faq.a6: Pingory supports multi-region checks through lightweight probe workers you deploy in any region (self-hosted), with majority-vote confirmation to reduce false positives — included from the Starter plan. The managed pingory.com service runs from a single region today.

cmp.meta.title: Pingory vs UptimeRobot 2026: Price, Limits & Honest Verdict
cmp.meta.desc: Pingory vs UptimeRobot 2026: an honest UptimeRobot alternative comparison — pricing, monitor limits, alerts, status pages, and where UptimeRobot still wins.
cmp.h1: Pingory vs UptimeRobot (2026): An Honest Comparison
cmp.verified: Last verified: September 2026. Prices are in USD.
cmp.lead: If you are looking for an UptimeRobot alternative, you are probably trying to keep an uptime monitor watching your sites, get alerted the moment one goes down, and avoid enterprise pricing. This page compares Pingory and UptimeRobot on the numbers that show up on an invoice — price, monitor limits, check intervals, alerts, and status pages. Both are real products with real users, and we will say plainly where UptimeRobot still wins.
cmp.short.1: Both services offer a free plan with 50 monitors at 5-minute checks and no credit card required.
cmp.short.2: Pingory's paid plans start at $4/month. UptimeRobot's start at $9–$10/month (Solo).
cmp.short.3: At $6/month, Pingory gives you unlimited monitors and 30-second checks. UptimeRobot's closest tier is $35–$41/month for 100 monitors.
cmp.short.4: UptimeRobot wins on scale and enterprise needs: 3M+ users since 2010, 4 selectable monitoring regions, SMS and voice alerts, SOC 2, and a much larger integration catalog.
cmp.short.5: Pingory wins on price per monitor, language coverage (8 UI languages), and a simpler, developer-focused product.
cmp.price.note: Prices below are the plans as published in September 2026. UptimeRobot discounts annual billing; Pingory's annual price is shown in parentheses. Verify current figures on each vendor's site before you buy.
cmp.tbl.r3: Status page on the free plan
cmp.tbl.r6: Fastest check on the cheapest paid plan
cmp.v.r2.p: HTTP/HTTPS and keyword checks, email alerts
cmp.v.r2.u: Website, port, ping and keyword checks; a basic status page; 5 integrations
cmp.v.r10.u: Scale — $77/mo, $65/mo billed yearly (200 monitors, 15-second checks; the 500-monitor tier is $179/$149)
cmp.v.r11.p: Public from $4; custom domain, white-label and password protection from $6
cmp.v.r11.u: Basic on free; custom domain from $9–$10; white-label and 100 pages from $35
cmp.v.r12.p: Email; plus Slack, Webhook and Telegram from $4; plus Discord, Microsoft Teams and PagerDuty from $6
cmp.v.r12.u: Email, SMS, voice call, mobile push and up to 12 integrations — SMS and voice credits are bought separately as top-ups (none included on Free)
cmp.v.r13.p: Self-hosted (Starter+): deploy probe workers in any region with majority-vote confirmation. Managed service: single region.
cmp.v.r13.u: 4 selectable regions (paid plans); North America only on Free
cmp.v.r14.p: 7 days free / 90 days Starter / 365 days Pro
cmp.v.r14.u: About 3 months free / 12 months Solo / 24 months Team and above
cmp.v.r15.p: 8, including Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Japanese and Korean
cmp.v.r17.u: SOC 2, DPA/MSA/SLA, dedicated CSM, custom invoicing
cmp.buy.p: On Pingory, $4/month (Starter) gets you 100 monitors, 60-second checks, all nine monitor types, four alert channels and a public status page. The equivalent capability on UptimeRobot — 60-second checks with the full set of monitor types — starts at Solo ($9–$10/month) with only 10 monitors, and reaching 100 monitors means Team ($35–$41), which also includes 30-second checks. Pingory's $6 Pro removes the monitor cap and drops checks to 30 seconds; UptimeRobot's 30-second tier starts at Team ($35+).
cmp.types.p: Both platforms cover the essentials: HTTP/HTTPS status, keyword content, ping (ICMP), TCP port, SSL certificate expiry, domain expiry, DNS records, API checks and heartbeat/cron monitoring. The difference is not which types exist — it is what you pay to unlock them. Pingory opens all nine from $4/month; UptimeRobot reserves most advanced types for tiers starting at $9–$10/month.
cmp.alerts.p: Email alerts are included on both, on every plan. Pingory adds Slack, Webhook and Telegram at $4, then Discord, Microsoft Teams and PagerDuty at $6. UptimeRobot offers more — including SMS and voice calls and a larger integration library — but SMS and voice are credit top-ups bought separately (none included on the free plan), and the free plan caps you at 5 integrations. If you need a phone call at 3 a.m., UptimeRobot is ahead; if email plus chat is enough, Pingory covers it for less.
cmp.sp.p: This is one of the clearest pricing gaps. Pingory includes a public status page with an incident timeline from $4/month, and unlocks custom domain, white-label, password protection and subscriber notifications at $6/month. UptimeRobot offers a basic version free, but a custom domain waits until Solo ($9–$10) and white-label requires Team ($35+).
cmp.iv.p: Free plans are identical at 5-minute checks. Pingory runs 60-second checks at $4 and 30-second checks at $6; UptimeRobot runs 60-second checks from $9–$10, 30-second from $35, and 15-second from $65–$77. On geography, UptimeRobot still leads for a hosted service — four selectable regions on paid plans (North America only on Free), versus Pingory's single managed region; Pingory's probe workers can run in any region only when self-hosted (Starter+).
cmp.lang.p: Pingory's interface ships in 8 languages, including Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Japanese and Korean. UptimeRobot's is primarily English. If you or your team work in a non-English language, especially in Latin America or Europe, that is a meaningful difference.
cmp.uw.h: Where UptimeRobot is still the better choice
cmp.uw.1: Scale and trust. UptimeRobot has been running since 2010 with 3M+ users monitoring millions of endpoints. Its track record and community are hard to match.
cmp.uw.2: Enterprise and compliance. SOC 2, DPA/MSA/SLA contracts, dedicated customer success and custom invoicing make it the safer pick for companies with procurement or compliance requirements.
cmp.uw.3: SMS and voice-call alerts, plus a much larger integration catalog (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, Mattermost, PagerDuty, Splunk On-Call, Zapier and more).
cmp.uw.4: Deeper free tier. A basic status page and more integration channels available without paying.
cmp.uw.close: If any of those are hard requirements for you, UptimeRobot is the right choice — and there is no shame in that.
cmp.pw.1: Price per monitor. A cheaper UptimeRobot alternative by a wide margin — $4 versus $9–$10 for comparable checks, and unlimited monitors at $6.
cmp.pw.2: Faster checks for less. 30-second checks at $6 versus $35+ elsewhere.
cmp.pw.3: Branding included early. Custom domain and white-label at $6 instead of $35+.
cmp.pw.5: A focused, uncluttered product built for indie developers and small projects, with honest limits and no metered surprises.
cmp.mig.p: Switching is low-friction. Pingory accepts UptimeRobot's export format directly — paste your exported monitor list and Pingory recreates your monitors automatically. Types your plan does not support are auto-downgraded to HTTP checks instead of failing, and any check interval below your plan's minimum is raised to the allowed value.
cmp.faq.q1: Is there a free UptimeRobot alternative?
cmp.faq.a1: Yes. Pingory's free plan includes 50 monitors with 5-minute checks and requires no credit card — the same headline limit as UptimeRobot's free tier.
cmp.faq.a2: Yes. Pingory's paid plans start at $4/month; UptimeRobot's start at $9–$10/month. For 100 monitors, that is $4 with 60-second checks on Pingory versus $35–$41 on UptimeRobot's Team plan, which includes 30-second checks.
cmp.faq.q3: Does Pingory include a status page?
cmp.faq.a3: Yes — a public one from $4/month, with custom domain, white-label and password protection at $6/month.
cmp.faq.q4: Can I move my existing monitors over?
cmp.faq.a4: Yes. Pingory imports UptimeRobot's export format directly, so you can migrate in a single paste.

cmpbs.meta.title: Pingory vs Better Stack 2026: Price, Simplicity & Honest Verdict
cmpbs.meta.desc: Pingory vs Better Stack 2026: an honest Better Stack alternative comparison — free plans, pricing per monitor, status pages, on-call features, and where Better Stack still wins.
cmpbs.h1: Pingory vs Better Stack (2026): An Honest Comparison
cmpbs.ogdesc: Pingory vs Better Stack 2026: pricing per monitor, status pages, on-call and log management compared — including where Better Stack still wins.
cmpbs.lead: If you are looking for a Better Stack alternative, you already know the product: Better Stack (formerly Better Uptime) is one of the most polished monitoring suites on the market, bundling uptime checks with incident management, on-call scheduling, and log management. This page compares Pingory and Better Stack on the numbers that show up on an invoice — price, monitor limits, check intervals, and status pages — and says plainly where Better Stack still wins.
cmpbs.short.1: Better Stack's free tier: 10 monitors at 3-minute checks plus 1 status page. Pingory's free tier: 50 monitors at 5-minute checks. Neither requires a credit card.
cmpbs.short.2: Pingory's paid plans start at $4/month for 100 monitors with 60-second checks. Better Stack's responder license starts around $29/month (annual billing), and 50 additional uptime monitors cost $21/month on top.
cmpbs.short.3: At $6/month, Pingory gives you unlimited monitors and 30-second checks. Better Stack's 30-second checks sit on its paid tiers.
cmpbs.short.4: Better Stack wins on incident management, on-call rotations with phone and SMS alerts, bundled log management, and a beautiful UI.
cmpbs.short.5: Pingory wins on price per monitor, status page economics, simplicity, 8 UI languages, and open source code (AGPL-3.0) you can self-host.
cmpbs.price.note: Prices below are as published in September 2026. Better Stack discounts annual billing and sells add-ons separately; verify current figures on each vendor's site before you buy.
cmpbs.v.r4.u: Team/Responder tiers with per-seat licenses + usage-based add-ons
cmpbs.v.r6.p: Included from $4/mo; custom domain, white-label and password protection at $6/mo
cmpbs.v.r6.u: 1 free page; additional public page $15/mo, private page $50/mo
cmpbs.v.r7.p: Not offered — Pingory focuses on uptime, not pager workflows
cmpbs.v.r7.u: Unlimited phone and SMS alerts with responder license, on-call schedules, escalations
cmpbs.v.r9.p: Email, Slack, Telegram, Discord, MS Teams, webhook, PagerDuty
cmpbs.v.r9.u: Email, Slack + many integrations; native phone/SMS on paid
cmpbs.tbl.note: Better Stack's free status page is genuinely useful and one of the reasons the product is popular — we say so plainly. The comparison above is about what happens when you outgrow the free tier.
cmpbs.bsw.p: If your outage response involves people being woken up, Better Stack is the stronger product. Its responder license includes unlimited phone and SMS alerts, on-call schedules, escalation policies and acknowledgement flows. It also bundles log management (the former Logtail product), session replay and error tracking — a real observability suite. And the UI is, frankly, excellent. If you are running a SaaS with a team and an on-call rotation, most of Better Stack's price buys exactly that.
cmpbs.pw.p: If what you actually need is uptime monitoring and a status page, Better Stack's pricing model means you are paying for an incident-management platform you may not use. Its responder license starts around $29/month per seat, and scaling monitors is usage-based on top of that. On Pingory, $4/month gets you 100 monitors at 60-second checks with a public status page included, and $6 removes the monitor cap entirely. Pingory is also open source under AGPL-3.0 — you can inspect the code or self-host it — and ships an interface in 8 languages.
cmpbs.types.p: Both cover the essentials: HTTP/HTTPS status, keyword content, ping, TCP port, SSL certificate expiry, DNS records, and heartbeat/cron monitoring. Pingory adds JSON/API assertions on every plan. Better Stack goes further at the high end with Playwright-based browser checks sold as metered minutes — a genuinely different capability class if you need user-journey testing.
cmpbs.faq.q1: Is there a free Better Stack alternative?
cmpbs.faq.a1: Yes. Pingory's free plan includes 50 monitors with 5-minute checks and requires no credit card. Better Stack's free tier includes 10 monitors at 3-minute checks plus one status page — better if you mainly want a free status page, worse on monitor count.
cmpbs.faq.q2: Is Pingory cheaper than Better Stack?
cmpbs.faq.a2: Yes. Pingory's paid plans start at $4/month for 100 monitors. On Better Stack, 50 additional uptime monitors cost $21/month — more than Pingory's entire Starter plan — before you even count the responder license that paid tiers are built around.
cmpbs.faq.a3: Yes — a public one from $4/month, with custom domain, white-label and password protection at $6/month. Better Stack includes one status page free; additional public pages cost $15/month and private pages $50/month.
cmpbs.faq.a4: Yes. Pingory is open source under AGPL-3.0 — clone it from GitHub and run it on your own server for free. Better Stack is a managed platform.
cmpbs.faq.q5: When is Better Stack the better choice?
cmpbs.faq.a5: When you need on-call schedules, phone/SMS alerting, escalation policies, or bundled log management. Pingory deliberately does not build pager workflows — if that is your requirement, Better Stack earns its price.

cmppd.tbl.note: Pingdom's price per monitor is the highest of the mainstream tools — roughly $1 per monitor per month on Starter. Pingory's Starter works out to about 4 cents.
cmppd.bsw.p: Pingdom is not trying to be a cheap uptime checker, and it shows. Its real user monitoring tracks how actual visitors experience your site, with geographic breakdowns, and its page-speed waterfall reports remain among the best in the industry. If your job is performance optimization of a high-traffic site — not just knowing when it is down — Pingdom's data is genuinely better, and Pingory does not offer an equivalent. It is also a 15-year-old brand with the enterprise procurement history to match.
cmppd.pw.p: If what you need is uptime monitoring with alerts and a status page, Pingdom's entry price is hard to justify: around $10–11/month for 10 monitors, with no free plan to evaluate the product first. Pingory gives you 50 monitors free forever, and $4/month gets you 100 monitors at 60-second checks with a public status page included — a capability Pingdom's core plans do not bundle. At $6 the monitor cap disappears and checks drop to 30 seconds. Pingory is also open source under AGPL-3.0, so you can self-host or inspect exactly what runs.
cmppd.types.p: Both cover HTTP/HTTPS status checks, keyword content checks, TCP port checks, SSL certificate expiry, DNS records, and heartbeat/cron monitoring. Pingory adds ping (ICMP) and JSON/API assertions on every plan. Pingdom goes further at the high end with browser-based transaction checks — multi-step user journeys — and the RUM and page-speed products described above.
cmppd.faq.q1: Is there a free Pingdom alternative?
cmppd.faq.a1: Yes. Pingory's free plan includes 50 monitors with 5-minute checks and no credit card. Pingdom offers a trial but no permanent free plan.
cmppd.faq.a2: Yes, by a wide margin. Pingory's paid plans start at $4/month for 100 monitors; Pingdom's Starter is around $10–11/month for 10 monitors. Ten times the monitors, at less than half the price.
cmppd.faq.a3: Yes — a public one from $4/month, with custom domain, white-label and password protection at $6/month. A comparable public status page is not part of Pingdom's core monitoring plans.
cmppd.faq.q4: Does Pingory offer real user monitoring?
cmppd.faq.a4: No — and this is where Pingdom wins. Pingory focuses on uptime, SSL, DNS, keyword, API and heartbeat monitoring. If you need RUM and page-speed waterfalls, Pingdom is the right tool and we will not pretend otherwise.
